title: Road Markings & Studs
whatItIs: Lines along the road tell you where you may cross, overtake and stop. As a rule, the more paint and the more solid the line, the stronger the message.

keyFacts.text: Chevrons bordered by a solid white line: you MUST NOT enter except in an emergency.
Yellow box: you MUST NOT enter until your exit road or lane is clear.

keyFacts: No stopping on roads with double white lines, even if your side is broken, except to drop off, pick up or load.
Double yellow lines: no waiting at any time, unless signs show seasonal restrictions.
A double red line ALWAYS means no stopping at any time.
Studs: white = lanes or centre, red = left edge, amber = central reservation, green = lay-bys and slip roads.

visual.caption: Double white lines: read the line nearest you

items.label: Centre line
items.meaning: Short lines, long gaps. Cross only to overtake or turn off, if clear.

items.label: Hazard warning line
items.meaning: Longer lines, shorter gaps: a hazard ahead.

items.label: Broken line nearest you
items.meaning: May cross to overtake if safe and you can finish before a solid line.

items.label: Solid line nearest you
items.meaning: MUST NOT cross or straddle it, except in the cases in Q1.

a.label: Hatching, broken border
points: Don't enter unless necessary and safe
Separates lanes or protects traffic turning right

b.label: Chevrons, solid border
points: MUST NOT enter except in an emergency
Used where slip roads leave and join motorways

onTheTest.question: The line nearest you in a set of double white lines is solid. When may you cross it, if the road is clear?
options: To overtake a cyclist travelling at 10 mph or less
To overtake a tractor travelling at 20 mph
To overtake any vehicle if you can see far ahead
To get a better view of the road ahead
onTheTest.why: Rule 129: you may cross to pass a stationary vehicle, or to overtake a pedal cycle, horse or road maintenance vehicle travelling at 10 mph or less, if the road is clear.

onTheTest.question: You want to turn right at a yellow box junction. When may you enter the box and wait?
options: When your exit is clear and only oncoming traffic stops you
Whenever the traffic lights are green
Only when the whole box is empty
Never: you must wait behind the box
onTheTest.why: Rule 174: you may wait in the box to turn right when only oncoming traffic, or vehicles waiting to turn right, stop you. Know Your Traffic Signs adds: only if the right-turn exit is clear.

traps: The 10 mph exception only covers pedal cycles, horses and road maintenance vehicles, not slow cars or tractors.
At a signalled roundabout you MUST NOT enter the box unless you can cross it completely without stopping.
Red and single yellow lines are only a guide: check the signs. No days shown? It applies every day.
